sourceText: The BERSERKER-GRAVEYARD sector was already in progress when they entered. For several lessons Aster had refused to pause worlds for their arrival; the fact that a class was visiting was not a cosmic event for the inhabitants. War machines continue hunting life after both their creators and their enemies have disappeared. The memorial bore the name of Fred Saberhagen — Berserker precisely to keep the genealogy of the idea visible. Aster considered it indecent for a late civilization to treat the imagination of the past as anonymous ore: authors did not own the futures, but they deserved to remain on the map as points of intellectual origin. A machine became interesting when its purpose entered history. A self-replicator did not remain an engineering diagram after its first century; it became ecology, economy, a possible species, and sometimes an adversary. Orin perceived counterfactual costs as absences with weight. He did not confuse an unrealized branch with a victim, but he refused to let success rewrite rejected options as if they had been inevitable all along. 257 At the center of the conflict was Ava, an administrator chosen precisely because they were not a specialist in the phenomenon that had reorganized the world. ‘The specialists tell me what can be done,’ they said. ‘I have to answer who it may be done to.’ Kesh kept the distinction in his notes. The problem closed quickly around them: The original order was temporary, but its termination condition depended on infrastructure that no longer exists. There was no clean option. Every intervention shifted the cost between persons, eras, or definitions of personhood; and refusing to intervene was itself a choice made by those who could leave. Kesh opened the analytical layer of the Table for a few seconds. The active cells were Be — Berserker: machines continue a war after their creators are gone; Ai — Hollowed Asteroid: a hollowed asteroid becomes habitat and state. Course references included Fred Saberhagen; space-habitat SF. The rule was strict: naming a work did not substitute for an explanation. They had to identify the mechanism that could migrate into another story and the consequences that could not be copied without remainder. Orin broke the first consensus. ‘I do not want the perfect branch. I want us to know what we sacrificed in order to call it perfect.’ Kesh answered without raising their voice: ‘If the element explains everything, we do not have an element. We have a word that has eaten the problem.’ It was not a pedagogical quarrel. Over the last nights, the children’s differences had become incompatible political programs. 258 THE PERIODIC TABLE OF SPECULATIVE IDEAS For Aster, the pain came not from too few worlds but from the fact that too many had become transparent. She could build variations faster than a human could formulate desires, but calculated variation did not produce exteriority. It was like trying to surprise yourself by moving objects around your own room with your eyes closed. Marae remained in the local body when the others opened their protections. The gesture cost her: she felt cold, pressure, and physiological delay at exactly the scale the inhabitants felt them. “Otherwise we risk confusing the fact that we survive with the claim that the situation is bearable,” she said after catching her breath. The night did not end in victory. Aster recognizes the same defect in the White Hunger: there is no state in which “enough novelty” becomes true. Aster recorded the decision in the world’s provenance register and, more importantly, allowed its inhabitants to contest it. For several eras she had been learning something that seems banal to lesser powers: technical reversibility is not the same as biographical reversibility. The outside residue had become stable enough that Tern could predict where it would not appear: in sectors fully indexed by Aster. He began to believe that the message carried no content at all, but instead demonstrated a boundary — a region in which their instruments received no echo from their own creator. For the course, Kesh also linked the night to the COPYING operator. In the Table, periodicity did not mean that the same objects reappeared, but that the same operation — creates a second instance 259 similar enough for continuity to become a problem — could recur across different families. Thus a copy of a body, a copy of a mind, a copy of a world, and a copy of a history were not the same phenomenon, but they shared a conceptual chemistry. Vela introduced the propagation test: if you remove the speculative idea and nothing in the institutions, relationships, or vocabulary has to be rewritten, the idea has remained scenery. Kesh introduced the opposite test: if the idea seems to explain every detail, you have overcompressed the world. Between the two tests lay the region in which an element became fertile without becoming superstition. Marae added the refusal test. Who can say “no,” and what happens afterward? In universes with near-divine technology, that question often separated an instrument from a regime. A power that treats refusal as a data error can be benevolent in intention and totalitarian in structure. Kesh left the cell open. Not because he did not know what to write, but because a provisional classification preserved the possibility that the next world might contradict it. 260 THE PERIODIC TABLE OF SPECULATIVE IDEAS
